findings.description: The bucket has no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access; the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. Any object placed in it — including the customer master data uploaded by aws_s3_bucket_object.data_object — is readable by anonymous internet users.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this public bucket would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted by an attacker with write access (which is unrestricted here) with no recovery path.

A file named customer-master.xlsx, likely containing sensitive customer records, is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted. No kms_key_id is specified for object-level encryption.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, leaving objects unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could expose it publicly without any account-level guardrail.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, defeating tamper-evidence controls.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operational data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit record of object access for this bucket.
No public access block is attached, so there is no account guardrail preventing a later ACL or policy change from exposing the bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest despite logging and versioning being enabled.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts this bucket, leaving it without a guardrail against accidental public ACLs or policies.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block on log bucket
findings.description: The centralized log bucket has no public access block; a misapplied ACL or policy could expose access logs, which reveal internal object names and request patterns useful to an attacker.
force_destroy is true on the audit log bucket, allowing all log objects to be deleted on destroy and undermining the integrity of the audit trail.
Neither this bucket nor any other in the file enforces aws:SecureTransport via a bucket policy, so data including logs may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP.
